ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p171/r4.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p171/r4.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p171/r4.claim: Every part of Sūrah al-Zukhruf relates deeply to its central theme, and the whole sūrah forms a harmonious unit from beginning to end.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p171/r4.anchor: each part of it is deeply related to its central theme

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p360#2/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p360#2/r6.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p360#2/r6.claim: بقدر means either by an eternal decree or in a sufficient measure, avoiding excess that corrupts and scarcity that fails to benefit.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p360#2/r6.anchor: بقدر: أي بقضاء وحتم في الأزل، أو بكفاية، لا كثيرا فيفسد، ولا قليلا فلا يجدي.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p360#2/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p360#2/r7.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p360#2/r7.claim: فأنشرنا means We revived with it.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p360#2/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p360#2/r8.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p360#2/r8.claim: ميتًا is masculine because it refers to rain, while بلدة is a collective noun.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p360#2/r8.anchor: بلدة ميتا: ذكر على معنى القطر، وبلدة اسم جنس.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p360#2/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p360#2/r9.speaker: أبو جعفر وعيسى
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p360#2/r9.claim: Abu Jaafar and Isa read ميتا with a doubled consonant; the majority read it without doubling.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p360#2/r9.anchor: وقرأ أبو جعفر وعيسى: ميتا بالتشديد.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p360#2/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p360#2/r10.speaker: الجمهور وابن وثاب وعبد الله بن جبير المصبح وعيسى وابن عامر والأخوان
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p360#2/r10.claim: The majority read تخرجون in the passive, while the named readers use the active voice.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p360#2/r10.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور: تخرجون: مبنيا للمفعول وابن وثاب، وعبد الله بن جبير المصبح، وعيسى، وابن عامر، والأخوان: مبنيا للفاعل.

STUDYQURAN:43:intro/r7.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:43:intro/r7.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:43:intro/r7.claim: The surah challenges the worldview of the Makkan idolaters, answering their objections and addressing forms of disbelief.
STUDYQURAN:43:intro/r7.anchor: The first half of the sūrah responds to different objections that the Makkan idolaters are reported to have posed to the message of the Quran

NAHHAS:v4p98/r8.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v4p98/r8.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v4p98/r8.claim: The kāf is accusative: you will be brought forth in an emergence like this.
NAHHAS:v4p98/r8.anchor: الكاف في موضع نصب أي تخرجون خروجا مثل ذلك

NAHHAS:v4p98/r9.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v4p98/r9.speaker: عبد الله بن مسعود
NAHHAS:v4p98/r9.claim: Ibn Masud says God sends rain like men's semen; remnants of earthly bodies sprout again, and flesh grows from soil and rain. Al-Nahhas says this is known only through transmitted revelation.
NAHHAS:v4p98/r9.anchor: وبين معنى هذا عبد الله بن مسعود وهو مما لا يؤخذ به إلا بالتوقيف قال

SAMIN-DURR:43:11/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:43:11/r1.speaker: العامة
SAMIN-DURR:43:11/r1.claim: The common reading lightens ميتا; ʿĪsā and Abū Jaʿfar read it with doubling.
SAMIN-DURR:43:11/r1.anchor: قرأه العامة مخففا. وعيسى وأبو جعفر مثقلا. وقد تقدم الكلام فيه في آل عمران.

SAMIN-DURR:43:11/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:43:11/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:43:11/r2.claim: The source refers back to an earlier discussion of the تخرجون readings in al-Aʿrāf.
SAMIN-DURR:43:11/r2.anchor: وتقدم في الأعراف الخلاف في تخرجون وتخرجون.

ASAD-NOTES:43:11#n9/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:43:11#n9/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:43:11#n9/r1.claim: The form nazzala indicates recurrence, hence Asad's rendering 'again and again'.
ASAD-NOTES:43:11#n9/r1.anchor: The grammatical form nazzala implies here recurrence: hence, "again and again".

NASHR:v2p223/r6.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p223/r6.speaker: أبو جعفر
NASHR:v2p223/r6.claim: Abū Jaʿfar doubles the yāʾ in all the listed forms of «الميتة/ميتا», «بلد ميت», and «الحي من الميت والميت من الحي».
NASHR:v2p223/r6.anchor: فقرأ أبو جعفر بتشديد الياء في جميع ذلك، ووافقه نافع في يس الأرض الميتة

NASHR:v2p267/r1.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p267/r1.speaker: حمزة، والكسائي، وخلف
NASHR:v2p267/r1.claim: Ḥamza, al-Kisāʾī, and Khalaf use fatḥ on the imperfect prefix and ḍamm on rāʾ in all four cited places; Yaʿqūb and Ibn Dhakwān agree at 7:25, and Ibn Dhakwān also agrees in al-Zukhruf.
NASHR:v2p267/r1.anchor: فقرأ حمزة والكسائي وخلف بفتح حرف المضارعة وضم الراء في الأربعة، وافقهم يعقوب وابن ذكوان هنا

NASHR:v2p267/r5.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p267/r5.speaker: زيد من طريق الصوري
NASHR:v2p267/r5.claim: Zayd through al-Ṣūrī is the sole Ibn Dhakwān route that reports the common ḍamm-tāʾ/fatḥ-rāʾ form at the Zukhruf occurrence.
NASHR:v2p267/r5.anchor: وبذلك انفرد عنه زيد من طريق الصوري في موضع الزخرف

QIRAAT-ER:43:11:13#1/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:43:11:13#1/r1.speaker: Gm
QIRAAT-ER:43:11:13#1/r1.claim: Gm's mutawātir form doubles yāʾ in mayyitan, a fuller adjective alongside maytan; both mean dead or lifeless, with greater phonetic weight.
QIRAAT-ER:43:11:13#1/r1.anchor: Variant with doubled yāʾ gives fuller adjective mayyitan beside standard maytan; semantic field remains dead/lifeless

QIRAAT-ER:43:11:16#1/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:43:11:16#1/r1.speaker: Pss
QIRAAT-ER:43:11:16#1/r1.claim: Pss's canonical active reading changes passive 'you are brought forth' to active or intransitive 'you come forth,' shifting agency while retaining kh-r-j.
QIRAAT-ER:43:11:16#1/r1.anchor: shifting emergence agency while keeping kh-r-j

ALUSI-FULL:v25p66#3/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v25p66#3/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v25p66#3/r5.claim: On Ibn al-Munir’s reading, the shift to ‘We brought forth’ in verse 11 falls naturally after a change of speaker; Moses’ speech followed by ‘We brought forth’ is a parallel.
ALUSI-FULL:v25p66#3/r5.anchor: ونظير ذلك قوله تعالى حكاية عن موسى عليه السلام : ( لا يضل ربي ولا ينسى )

ALUSI-FULL:v25p67/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v25p67/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v25p67/r1.claim: Rain falls in a measure set by divine will, wisdom, and interests; only God knows precisely how much falls each year.
ALUSI-FULL:v25p67/r1.anchor: أي بمقدار تقتضيه المشيئة المبنية على الحكم والمصالح ولا يعلم مقدار ما ينزل

ALUSI-FULL:v25p67/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v25p67/r2.speaker: البحر
ALUSI-FULL:v25p67/r2.claim: Al-Bahr glosses the measure as a decree fixed in pre-eternity; Alusi prefers the measure determined by divine wisdom.
ALUSI-FULL:v25p67/r2.anchor: وفي البحر بقدر أي بقضاء وحتم في الأزل والأول أولى

ALUSI-FULL:v25p67/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v25p67/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v25p67/r3.claim: Alusi doubts claims that the contemporary ‘audometer’ precisely measures annual rainfall even in one small locality, much less everywhere.
ALUSI-FULL:v25p67/r3.anchor: المسماة بالاود وميتر يزعمون أنه يعرف بها مقدار المطر النازل في كل بلد

ALUSI-FULL:v25p67/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v25p67/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v25p67/r4.claim: God revived the barren town by the rain; it had no growth or plants at all.

ALUSI-FULL:v25p67/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v25p67/r5.speaker: أبو جعفر وعيسى
ALUSI-FULL:v25p67/r5.claim: Abu Jaafar and Isa read ‘mayyitan’ with doubled yāʾ; the masculine form treats ‘town’ as land or place.
ALUSI-FULL:v25p67/r5.anchor: بالتشديد وتذكيره لأن البلدة في معنى البلد والمكان

ALUSI-FULL:v25p67/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v25p67/r6.speaker: الجلبي
ALUSI-FULL:v25p67/r6.claim: Al-Jalabi suggests that the feminine ‘town’ with masculine ‘dead’ may signal the extreme limit of its lifelessness; Alusi says this is possible.
ALUSI-FULL:v25p67/r6.anchor: قال الجلبي : لا يبعد والله تعالى أعلم أن يكون تأنيث البلد

ALUSI-FULL:v25p67/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v25p67/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v25p67/r7.claim: The description of the town as dead uses either an implicit or explicit metaphor.
ALUSI-FULL:v25p67/r7.anchor: وفي الكلام استعارة مكنية أو تصريحية

ALUSI-FULL:v25p67/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v25p67/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v25p67/r8.claim: The shift to first-person plural highlights divine care for reviving the earth and signals the act’s importance.
ALUSI-FULL:v25p67/r8.anchor: إلى نون العظمة لإظهار كمال العناية بأمر الأحياء والأشعار بعظم خطره

ALUSI-FULL:v25p67/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v25p67/r9.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v25p67/r9.claim: As vegetation emerges from the earth, people will be raised alive from their graves; ‘likewise’ modifies an omitted verbal noun meaning resurrection like this.
ALUSI-FULL:v25p67/r9.anchor: أيتبعثون من قبوركم أحياء وفي التعبير عن إخراج النبات

ALUSI-FULL:v25p67/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v25p67/r10.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v25p67/r10.claim: Calling plant growth ‘revival’ and resurrection ‘being brought forth’ magnifies vegetation and makes resurrection seem less difficult, rebutting deniers.
ALUSI-FULL:v25p67/r10.anchor: تفخيم لشأن الأنبات وتهوين لأمرالبعث وفي ذلك من الرد على منكر ما فيه

ALUSI-FULL:v25p67/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v25p67/r11.speaker: ابن وثاب وعبد الله بن جبير وعيسى وابن عامر والأخوان
ALUSI-FULL:v25p67/r11.claim: These readers pronounce ‘tukhrajūn’ in the active voice.
ALUSI-FULL:v25p67/r11.anchor: وقرأ ابن وثاب وعبد الله بن جبير وعيسى وابن عامر والأخوان ( تخرجون ) مبنيا للفاعل

BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p207/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p207/r3.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p207/r3.claim: Rain is sent in proportion to people's need, unlike the unmeasured flood sent on Noah's people that destroyed them.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p207/r3.anchor: والذي نزل من السماء ماء بقدر} أي بقدر حاجتكم إليه لا كما أنزل على قوم نوح بغير قدر حتى أهلكهم.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p207/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p207/r4.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p207/r4.claim: Just as rain revives a dead town, people will be brought alive from their graves.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p207/r4.anchor: فأنشرنا به بلدة ميتا كذلك} أي كما أحيينا هذه البلدة [الميتة] (1) بالمطر كذلك، {تخرجون} من قبوركم أحياء.

BAYDAWI-FULL:43:10-13/r3.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:43:10-13/r3.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:43:10-13/r3.claim: Rain is sent in an amount that benefits and does no harm.
BAYDAWI-FULL:43:10-13/r3.anchor: ماء بقدر } بمقدار ينفع ولا يضر

BAYDAWI-FULL:43:10-13/r4.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:43:10-13/r4.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:43:10-13/r4.claim: بلدة takes a masculine adjective because it can mean البلد or المكان, both masculine.
BAYDAWI-FULL:43:10-13/r4.anchor: وتذكيره لأن البلدة بمعنى البلد والمكان

BAYDAWI-FULL:43:10-13/r5.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:43:10-13/r5.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:43:10-13/r5.claim: As the dead land is revived, people will be raised from their graves.
BAYDAWI-FULL:43:10-13/r5.anchor: كذلك } مثل ذلك الإنشار. { تخرجون } تنشرون من قبوركم

BAYDAWI-FULL:43:10-13/r6.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:43:10-13/r6.speaker: ابن عامر وحمزة والكسائي
BAYDAWI-FULL:43:10-13/r6.claim: Ibn Amir, Hamza, and al-Kisa'i read تخرجون with open تاء and damma on راء.
BAYDAWI-FULL:43:10-13/r6.anchor: وقرأ ابن عامر وحمزة والكسائي { تخرجون } بفتح التاء وضم الراء

BIQAI-FULL:v7p9/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p9/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v7p9/r4.claim: The repeated relative pronoun emphasizes the greatness of the agent and signals that resurrection, evidenced by rain and revival, is a greater sign than the earth’s stability and roads.
BIQAI-FULL:v7p9/r4.anchor: وبإعادة الموصول الدال على الفاعل المذكر بعظمته

BIQAI-FULL:v7p9/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p9/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v7p9/r5.claim: God sends fresh water gradually from above, in an amount suited to people’s needs and beneficial without harm; it serves crops, fruit, and drinking for people and livestock.
BIQAI-FULL:v7p9/r5.anchor: أي بحسب التدريج , ولولا قدرته الباهرة

BIQAI-FULL:v7p9/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p9/r6.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v7p9/r6.claim: أنشرنا means revived; its underlying semantic range turns on motion, extension, and spreading out.
BIQAI-FULL:v7p9/r6.anchor: أي أحيينا , والمادة تدور على الحركة

BIQAI-FULL:v7p9/r7.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p9/r7.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v7p9/r7.claim: The dead town is a place people inhabit and work to sustain, whose vegetation dried up while its inhabitants lacked the means to irrigate it.
BIQAI-FULL:v7p9/r7.anchor: أي مكانا يجتمع الناس فيه للإقامة

BIQAI-FULL:v7p9/r8.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p9/r8.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v7p9/r8.claim: Calling it dead depicts extreme barrenness: weak soil and inhabitants, drought, and the disappearance of its former vegetation.
BIQAI-FULL:v7p9/r8.anchor: العضف والموت بلغ الغاية بضعف أرضه في نفسها

BIQAI-FULL:v7p9/r9.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p9/r9.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v7p9/r9.claim: Plant revival and resurrection are alike within God’s power: he can restore disintegrated human bodies with their spirits, matter, and attributes; water itself has no power apart from his measure.
BIQAI-FULL:v7p9/r9.anchor: من أجساد الآدميين وإخراجه كما كان بروحه وجميع جواهره وأعراضه

BIQAI-FULL:v7p9/r10.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p9/r10.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v7p9/r10.claim: Just as plants emerge from the dead earth, people will be brought out of bodily death; they also emerge from ignorance into faith and become wise and knowing.
BIQAI-FULL:v7p9/r10.anchor: من الموت الحسي والمعنوي بأيسر أمر من أمره تعالى

BIQAI-FULL:v7p10/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p10/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v7p10/r1.claim: The author links people’s emergence from death with the verse’s image of humans spreading across the earth, then extends the image to emergence from ignorance into faith.
BIQAI-FULL:v7p10/r1.anchor: وتخرجون من ظلمة الجهل إلى نور الإيمان فإذا أنتم حكماء عالمون

IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p168/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p168/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p168/r6.claim: The eleven second-person pronouns across these four verses follow the expected address and are not iltifat.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p168/r6.anchor: وضمائر الخطاب الأحد عشر الواقعة في الآيات الأربع من قوله : { الذي جعل لكم الأرض مهادا }

IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p171/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p171/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p171/r1.claim: إنشاء means reviving, as in 80:22; the causative hamza in أنشره derives from نشر, to revive, while نشر originally means spreading what was folded.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p171/r1.anchor: والإنشاء : الإحياء كما في قوله : { ثم إذا شاء أنشره } ( عبس : 22 )

IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p171/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p171/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p171/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas objected to the reading كيف ننشرها with fatḥa on nūn and ḍamma on shīn, citing ثم إذا شاء أنشره.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p171/r2.anchor: وعن ابن عباس أنه أنكر على من قرأ

IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p171/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p171/r3.speaker: الأعشى
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p171/r3.claim: Al-A'sha's verse calls a dead person الناشر, witnessing نشر for revival; the root originally means spreading the folded and developed into revival and dispersal.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p171/r3.anchor: قال الأعشى : حتى يقول الناس مما رأوا

IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p171/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p171/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p171/r4.claim: Calling earth's revival نشر is metaphorical, since reviving earth is itself figurative; the usage aptly anticipates resurrection.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p171/r4.anchor: والنشر هنا مجاز لأن الإحياء للأرض مجاز

IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p171/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p171/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p171/r5.claim: The pronoun in أنشرنا shifts from speaking of God in the third person to the first-person plural.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p171/r5.anchor: وضمير { فأنشرنا } التفات من الغيبة إلى التكلم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p171/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p171/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p171/r6.claim: ميت is opposite to living, and describing a town with the masculine form is conventional figurative usage.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p171/r6.anchor: والميت ضد الحي . ووصف البلدة به مجاز شائع

IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p171/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p171/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p171/r7.claim: ميت lacks feminine marking because it follows adjective forms originating as verbal nouns, such as عدل and زور; the town is only figuratively feminine.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p171/r7.anchor: لكونه على زنة الوصف الذي أصله مصدر نحو : عدل وزور فحسن تجريده من علامة التأنيث

IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p171/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p171/r8.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p171/r8.claim: The parenthetical resurrection statement digresses from proofs of exclusive divinity to establish resurrection and rebut those deeming it impossible; كذلك points to the earth's revival.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p171/r8.anchor: وجملة { كذلك تخرجون } معترضة بين المتعاطفين

IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p171/r9.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p171/r9.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p171/r9.claim: The likeness is bringing the living after death; the simile shows resurrection is possible, as illustrated by Abu al-Tayyib's comparison of musk with deer blood.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p171/r9.anchor: المقصود من التشبيه إظهار إمكان المشبه كقول أبي الطيب

IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p171/r10.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p171/r10.speaker: الجمهور
IBNASHUR-FULL:v25p171/r10.claim: The majority read تخرجون in the passive; Hamza, al-Kisa'i, and Ibn Dhakwan from Ibn Amir read it active, with the same meaning.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p47#2/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p47#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p47#2/r1.claim: These descriptions of God's acts are blessings to humanity and proof against every disbelieving polytheist.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p47#2/r1.anchor: على كل كافر مشرك بالله تعالى.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p47#2/r8.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p47#2/r8.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p47#2/r8.claim: The water sent down from heaven refers by consensus to rain.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p47#2/r8.anchor: من السماء هو المطر بإجماع، واختلف المتأولون

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p47#2/r9.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p47#2/r9.speaker: فرقة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p47#2/r9.claim: One group takes the measured sending as a decree fixed in eternity.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p47#2/r9.anchor: فقالت فرقة معناه: بقضاء وحتم في الأزل.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p47#2/r10.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p47#2/r10.speaker: آخرون
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p47#2/r10.claim: Others understand an amount sufficient for well-being: neither so much that it ruins nor so little that it fails.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p47#2/r10.anchor: وقال آخرون المعنى: بقدر في الكفاية للصلاح لا إكثار فيفسد ولا قلة فيقصر،

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p47#2/r11.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p47#2/r11.speaker: فرقة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p47#2/r11.claim: Another group reads it as a specified, carefully determined quantity.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p47#2/r11.anchor: وقالت فرقة معناه: بتقدير وتحرير، أي قدرا معلوما،

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p47#2/r12.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p47#2/r12.speaker: بعضهم
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p47#2/r12.claim: Some who take it as specified say the same total descends each year, though its location varies.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p47#2/r12.anchor: فقال بعضهم: ينزل كل عام ماء قدرا واحدا لا يفضل عام عاما،

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p47#2/r13.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p47#2/r13.speaker: فرقة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p47#2/r13.claim: Another group says the amount differs from year to year according to God's prior decree.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p47#2/r13.anchor: وقالت فرقة: بل ينزل الله تقديرا ما في عام، وينزل في آخر تقديرا آخر بحسب ما سبق به قضاؤه،

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p47#2/r14.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p47#2/r14.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p47#2/r14.claim: Ansharna means that God brought the dead land back to life; the verb can mean that the dead person revived or God revived him.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p47#2/r14.anchor: و: «أنشرنا» معناه: أحيينا، يقال: نشر الميت، وأنشره الله.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p47#2/r15.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p47#2/r15.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p47#2/r15.claim: Balda is generic and takes masculine maytan because it denotes a region and its feminine gender is not real.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p47#2/r15.anchor: بلدة اسم جنس، ووصفها ب ميتا دون ضمير من حيث هي واقعة موقع قطر ونحوه،

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p47#2/r16.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p47#2/r16.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p47#2/r16.claim: Most readers have maytan with a quiescent ya; Abu Jaafar and Isa ibn Umar read it with a doubled kasra ya; Ibn Atiyya prefers the first as resembling forms such as زور and عدل.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p47#2/r16.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور: «ميتا» بسكون الياء. وقرأ أبو جعفر بن القعقاع: «ميتا» بياء مكسورة مشددة،

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p47#3/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p47#3/r1.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p47#3/r1.claim: Most of the Seven, al-Araj, and Abu Jaafar read passive تُخرجون; Hamza, al-Kisai, Ibn Wathab, and Abd Allah ibn Jubayr al-Musayyih read active تخرجون.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p47#3/r1.anchor: وقرأ أكثر السبعة والأعرج وأبو جعفر: «كذلك تخرجون» بضم التاء وفتح الراء. وقرأ حمزة

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p304/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p304/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p304/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas says the rain was sent in measured quantity, unlike the unmeasured flood sent upon Noah's people, so it would benefit people.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p304/r1.anchor: قال ابن عباس يريد انه ليس كما أنزل على قوم نوح بغير قدر فأغرقهم بل هو بقدر ليكون نافعا

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p304/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p304/r3.speaker: حمزة والكسائي وابن عامر
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p304/r3.claim: Hamza, al-Kisa'i, and Ibn Amir read with fatḥa on the tāʾ and ḍamma on the rāʾ; the other readers use ḍamma on tāʾ and fatḥa on rāʾ.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p304/r3.anchor: قرأ حمزة والكسائي وابن عامر تخرجون بفتح التاء وضم الراء والباقون بضم التاء وفتح الراء

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p219#2/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p219#2/r4.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p219#2/r4.claim: Rain is sent in a measured amount sufficient for crops, fruits and drinking water for people and livestock.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p219#2/r4.anchor: أي: بحسب الكفاية لزروعكم (1) وثماركم وشربكم، لأنفسكم ولأنعامكم.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p219#2/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p219#2/r5.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p219#2/r5.claim: Water revives dead land, making it swell and rise and grow every beautiful kind; this revival points to God raising bodies after their death.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p219#2/r5.anchor: أي: أرضا ميتة، فلما جاءها الماء اهتزت وربت، وأنبتت من كل زوج بهيج.

BURSEVI:v8p271#2/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p271#2/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p271#2/r1.claim: God ordinarily sends beneficial measured rain without flooding or falling short of agricultural need; damaging floods may occur every twenty or thirty years as trial and requital.
BURSEVI:v8p271#2/r1.anchor: بمقدار ووزن ينفع العباد والبلاد ، ولا يضرهم

BURSEVI:v8p271#3/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p271#3/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p271#3/r1.claim: Ansharna means God revived by the water; nashr is reviving the dead.
BURSEVI:v8p271#3/r1.anchor: أحيينا بذلك الماء والإنشار إحياء الميت

BURSEVI:v8p271#3/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p271#3/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p271#3/r2.claim: Mayta is a shortened form of mayyit and describes land barren of growth; barrenness is likened to bodily death.
BURSEVI:v8p271#3/r2.anchor: {بلدة ميتا} مخفف من الميت بالتشديد ؛ أي : خالية عن النماء والنبات بالكلية شبه زوال النماء عنها بزوال الحياة عن البدن

BURSEVI:v8p271#3/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p271#3/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p271#3/r3.claim: Mayta is masculine because balda is understood as balad, place, or open space.
BURSEVI:v8p271#3/r3.anchor: وتذكير ميتا ؛ لأن البلدة في معنى البلد ، والمكان والفضاء.

BURSEVI:v8p271#3/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p271#3/r4.speaker: سعدي المفتي
BURSEVI:v8p271#3/r4.claim: Saʿdi al-Mufti suggests the gender contrast signals the land's extreme weakness and the plural verb stresses God's care in reviving it.
BURSEVI:v8p271#3/r4.anchor: وقال سعدي المفتي : لا يبعد والله تعالى أعلم أن يكون تأنيث البلد وتذكير الميت إشارة إلى بلوغ ضعف حاله الغاية

BURSEVI:v8p271#3/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p271#3/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p271#3/r5.claim: As God revives dead land by bringing forth plants, He raises people alive from their graves; the analogy establishes His power and wisdom.
BURSEVI:v8p271#3/r5.anchor: أي : مثل ذلك الإحياء الذي هو في الحقيقة إخراج النبات من الأرض

BURSEVI:v8p271#3/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p271#3/r6.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p271#3/r6.claim: Calling plant growth revival and resurrection merely bringing out magnifies germination and makes resurrection seem easy, strengthening the analogy.
BURSEVI:v8p271#3/r6.anchor: وفي التعبير عن إخراج النبات بالإنشار الذي هو إحياء الموتى ، وعن إحيائهم بالإخراج تفخيم لشأن الإنبات وتهوين لأمر البعث

BURSEVI:v8p271#3/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p271#3/r7.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p271#3/r7.claim: The spirit's sky sends guidance like rain to revive the dead heart, moving the servant from existential darkness into God's light.
BURSEVI:v8p271#3/r7.anchor: وفي الآية إشارة إلى أن الله تعالى : نزل من سماء الروح ماء الهداية ، فأحيا به بلدة القلب الميت

BURSEVI:v8p271#3/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p271#3/r8.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p271#3/r8.claim: As a seed cannot emerge until rain gives it life underground, a servant cannot leave existential darkness until guidance revives the heart.
BURSEVI:v8p271#3/r8.anchor: كما أن البذر ما لم يحيا في داخل الأرض بالمطر لم يظهر في ظاهرها

BURSEVI:v8p271#3/r9.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p271#3/r9.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p271#3/r9.claim: Hasan al-Basri's mother served Umm Salama; when the child cried in his mother's absence, Umm Salama nursed him, and his wisdom and eloquence were attributed to her blessing.
BURSEVI:v8p271#3/r9.anchor: روي : أن أم الحسن البصري رضي الله عنه كانت مولاة أم سلمة رضي الله عنها زوجة النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

BURSEVI:v8p271#3/r10.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p271#3/r10.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p271#3/r10.claim: Lawful nourishment is another means by which the heart comes alive.
BURSEVI:v8p271#3/r10.anchor: حياة القلب بأسباب منها : الغذاء الحلال.

BURSEVI:v8p271#3/r11.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p271#3/r11.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p271#3/r11.claim: Uways al-Qarani refused a found dinar as possibly stolen; a sheep then brought him food and identified it as God's provision.
BURSEVI:v8p271#3/r11.anchor: اويس القرنى رضي الله عنه يكبارسه شبا نروز هيج نخورده بود بيرون آمد برراه يك دينار افتاده بود

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p242#2/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p242#2/r2.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p242#2/r2.claim: The words We revived a dead land and the descriptions following the pagans’ admission are God’s speech, not theirs.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p242#2/r2.anchor: هو من قول الله لا من قولهم

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p242#2/r3.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p242#2/r3.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p242#2/r3.claim: Rain comes in an amount that keeps lands and people safe rather than causing a flood.

MUQATIL:43:11-13/r1.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:43:11-13/r1.speaker: author
MUQATIL:43:11-13/r1.claim: The measured water from heaven is rain.
MUQATIL:43:11-13/r1.anchor: والذي نزل من السماء ماء بقدر } ، وهو المطر

MUQATIL:43:11-13/r2.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:43:11-13/r2.speaker: author
MUQATIL:43:11-13/r2.claim: God revived a dead, barren town with water and plants grew there; people likewise emerge from the earth as plants.
MUQATIL:43:11-13/r2.anchor: فأحيينا به، يعني بالماء بلدة ميتا لا نبت فيها، فلما أصابها الماء أنبتت

NASAFI-FULL:v4p109#8/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p109#8/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p109#8/r1.claim: God sends rain in a measured amount that sustains people and supplies the lands' needs.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p109#8/r1.anchor: ﴿ والذي نزل من السماء ماء بقدر ﴾ بمقدار

NASAFI-FULL:v4p109#8/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p109#8/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p109#8/r2.claim: Ansharnā means We revived; the narration shifts from speaking of God in the third person to first person because the listener recognizes the referent.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p109#8/r2.anchor: فأحيينا عدول من المغايبة إلى الاخبار لعلم المخاطب بالمراد

NASAFI-FULL:v4p109#8/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p109#8/r3.speaker: يزيد
NASAFI-FULL:v4p109#8/r3.claim: Yazīd reads the adjective as mayyitan, masculine, agreeing with the town understood as a place.

NASAFI-FULL:v4p109#8/r4.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p109#8/r4.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p109#8/r4.claim: Likewise, you will be brought out of your graves alive; Ḥamza and ʿAlī read the verb as recorded here.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p109#8/r4.anchor: من قبوركم أحياء تخرجون حمزة وعلى

NASAFI-FULL:v4p109#8/r5.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p109#8/r5.speaker: أبو حاتم
NASAFI-FULL:v4p109#8/r5.claim: There is no pause at al-ʿAlīm because alladhī qualifies it; Abū Ḥātim allows a pause by supplying huwa before alladhī.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p109#8/r5.anchor: ولا وقف على العليم لأن الذى صفته وقد وقف عليه أبو حاتم على تقديره هو الذى

NASAFI-FULL:v4p109#8/r6.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p109#8/r6.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p109#8/r6.claim: The descriptive clauses are not the polytheists' own words, since they denied resurrection; the verse argues against their denial by affirming resurrection.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p109#8/r6.anchor: بل الآية حجة عليهم في انكار البعث

QURTUBI-FULL:43:11/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:43:11/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:43:11/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas says the rain was measured: unlike the flood sent on Noah's people, it neither overwhelms and drowns nor falls short, but sustains people and their livestock.
QURTUBI-FULL:43:11/r1.anchor: قال ابن عباس: أي لا كما أنزل على قوم نوح بغير قدر حتى أغرقهم، بل هو بقدر لا طوفان مغرق ولا قاصر عن الحاجة

QURTUBI-FULL:43:11/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:43:11/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:43:11/r2.claim: Ansharna means We revived, and by it means by the water; the dead town is barren and empty of vegetation.
QURTUBI-FULL:43:11/r2.anchor: { فأنشرنا } أي أحيينا. { به } أي بالماء. { بلدة ميتا } أي مقفرة من النبات

QURTUBI-FULL:43:11/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:43:11/r3.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:43:11/r3.claim: People will likewise be brought out of their graves, because the One able to revive land is able to resurrect them.
QURTUBI-FULL:43:11/r3.anchor: أي من قبوركم لأن من قدر على هذا قدر على ذلك

QURTUBI-FULL:43:11/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:43:11/r4.speaker: يحيى بن وثاب والأعمش وحمزة والكسائي وابن ذكوان عن ابن عامر
QURTUBI-FULL:43:11/r4.claim: Yahya ibn Waththab, al-A'mash, Hamza, al-Kisa'i and Ibn Dhakwan from Ibn Amir read the active form يخرجون; the others read the passive.
QURTUBI-FULL:43:11/r4.anchor: وقرأ يحيى بن وثاب والأعمش وحمزة والكسائي وابن ذكوان عن ابن عامر «يخرجون» بفتح الياء وضم الراء. الباقون على الفعل المجهول

RAZI-FULL:v27p169/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v27p169/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v27p169/r3.claim: Razi raises whether rain literally descends from heaven or from clouds, which are called heaven because whatever is elevated is heaven; he says this question was discussed at length earlier.
RAZI-FULL:v27p169/r3.anchor: ظاهر هذه الآية يقتضي أن الماء ينزل من السماء ، فهل الأمر كذلك أو يقال إنه ينزل من السحاب

RAZI-FULL:v27p169/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v27p169/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v27p169/r4.claim: Rain falls in the amount each region needs, neither excess nor shortage, unlike the unmeasured flood sent on Noah's people, and thereby sustains people and livestock.
RAZI-FULL:v27p169/r4.anchor: إنما ينزل من السماء بقدر ما يحتاج إليه أهل تلك البقعة من غير زيادة ولا نقصان لا كما أنزل على قوم نوح بغير قدر

RAZI-FULL:v27p169/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v27p169/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v27p169/r5.claim: A dead town is one barren of vegetation; God revives it, which is what “spreading life” means here.
RAZI-FULL:v27p169/r5.anchor: أي خالية من النبات فأحييناها وهو الإنشار

RAZI-FULL:v27p169/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v27p169/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v27p169/r6.claim: Reviving dead land demonstrates God's power and wisdom and thus His ability to resurrect people after death, as He revives the earth.
RAZI-FULL:v27p169/r6.anchor: هذا الدليل كما يدل على قدرة الله وحكمته فكذلك يدل على قدرته على البعث والقيامة

RAZI-FULL:v27p169/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v27p169/r7.speaker: بعضهم
RAZI-FULL:v27p169/r7.claim: Some say the likeness is that God will recreate and bring people from the earth using water like semen, as rain makes plants grow; Razi calls this weak because the wording only asserts resurrection.
RAZI-FULL:v27p169/r7.anchor: وقال بعضهم بل وجه التشبيه أن يعيدهم ويخرجهم من الأرض بماء كالمني كما تنبت الأرض بماء المطر

STUDYQURAN:43:11/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:43:11/r1.speaker: some commentators
STUDYQURAN:43:11/r1.claim: Water sent in due measure suffices to sustain people, livestock, and crops, and is not ordinarily a deluge like the flood in Noah's time.
STUDYQURAN:43:11/r1.anchor: God sends water sufficient to sustain people, livestock, and crops (IK) and does not usually send down a deluge (JJ)

STUDYQURAN:43:11/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:43:11/r2.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:43:11/r2.claim: The Quran elsewhere says God created everything and measured it out; the theological significance of measure is discussed at 54:49.
STUDYQURAN:43:11/r2.anchor: Elsewhere it is said that God created everything, then measured it out with due measure

STUDYQURAN:43:11/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:43:11/r3.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:43:11/r3.claim: Reviving dead land is used here and elsewhere as a metaphor for human resurrection.
STUDYQURAN:43:11/r3.anchor: The last line of the present verse is one of several places where the Quran employs the revivification of dead land as a metaphor for the resurrection of human beings

STUDYQURAN:43:11/r4.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:43:11/r4.speaker: some commentators
STUDYQURAN:43:11/r4.claim: The image also symbolizes the death and life of the soul.
STUDYQURAN:43:11/r4.anchor: Such imagery is also understood as a spiritual allegory and symbol for the death and life of the soul

TAB-FULL:v20p554#2/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v20p554#2/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v20p554#2/r1.claim: Allah sends rain in the amount people need: neither a destructive flood like Noah’s nor too little to grow crops, but life-giving rain.
TAB-FULL:v20p554#2/r1.anchor: بمقدار حاجتكم إليه، فلم يجعله كالطوفان، فيكون عذابا كالذي أنزل على قوم نوح، ولا جعله قليلا لا ينبت به النبات والزرع

TAB-FULL:v20p554#2/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v20p554#2/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v20p554#2/r2.claim: The dead town is a barren place without plants or crops, dried out and devastated by drought; Allah revives it with rain.
TAB-FULL:v20p554#2/r2.anchor: فأحيينا به بلدة من بلادكم ميتا، يعني مجدبة لا نبات بها ولا زرع، قد درست من الجدوب، وتعفنت من القحوط

TAB-FULL:v20p554#2/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v20p554#2/r3.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v20p554#2/r3.claim: Just as rain brings plants and crops from a dead land, people will be raised after decay in the earth, restored alive to their former bodily form.
TAB-FULL:v20p554#2/r3.anchor: كذلك أيها الناس تخرجون من بعد فنائكم ومصيركم في الأرض رفاتا بالماء الذي أنزله إليها لإحيائكم من بعد مماتكم منها أحياء كهيئتكم التي بها قبل مماتكم

TAB-FULL:v20p554#2/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v20p554#2/r4.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v20p554#2/r4.claim: Qatāda compares the resurrection on Judgment Day to Allah’s revival of the dead earth with rain.
TAB-FULL:v20p554#2/r4.anchor: عن قتادة، {والذي نزل من السماء ماء بقدر} [الزخرف: 11] الآية، «كما أحيا الله هذه الأرض الميتة بهذا الماء كذلك تبعثون يوم القيامة»

TAB-FULL:v20p554#2/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v20p554#2/r5.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v20p554#2/r5.claim: Ansharnā means We brought to life; Arabs also say the earth was revived as nushirat, as al-Aʿshā’s verse calls the dead person al-nāshir.
TAB-FULL:v20p554#2/r5.anchor: كما قال الأعشى: حتى يقول الناس مما رأوا … يا عجبا للميت الناشر

TABATABAI:43:11-14/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:43:11-14/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:43:11-14/r1.claim: Rain is measured to show that it comes through intention and governance, not by chance.
TABATABAI:43:11-14/r1.anchor: قيد تنزيل الماء بقدر للإشارة إلى أنه عن إرادة وتدبير

TABATABAI:43:11-14/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:43:11-14/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:43:11-14/r2.claim: Anshara means to bring to life; mayyit is the lighter form of the intensified mayyit, and a town is described as dead because it is a place.

TABATABAI:43:11-14/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:43:11-14/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:43:11-14/r3.claim: The shift to first-person plural in ‘We revived’ signals special attention.
TABATABAI:43:11-14/r3.anchor: والالتفات عن الغيبة إلى التكلم مع الغير في { أنشرنا }

TABATABAI:43:11-14/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:43:11-14/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:43:11-14/r4.claim: Measured rain and revival show God’s creation and governance, from which the verse infers resurrection: people will be raised alive from their graves as the dead land was revived.
TABATABAI:43:11-14/r4.anchor: ولما استدل بتنزيل الماء بقدر وإحياء البلدة الميتة على خلقه وتدبيره

TABATABAI:43:11-14/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:43:11-14/r5.speaker: قيل
TABATABAI:43:11-14/r5.claim: One explanation says describing plants as revived and people as brought forth magnifies plant growth and makes resurrection seem easy, clarifying the analogy.
TABATABAI:43:11-14/r5.anchor: قيل في التعبير عن إخراج النبات بالانشار الذي هو إحياء الموتى

TABRISI:43:11-14/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:43:11-14/r1.speaker: author
TABRISI:43:11-14/r1.claim: Anshara means God brought creatures back to life; al-A'sha's verse about a dead person revived on a woman's breast illustrates “resurrected.”
TABRISI:43:11-14/r1.anchor: أي أحياهم فحيوا قال الأعشى: لو أسندت ميتا إلى نحرها

TABRISI:43:11-14/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:43:11-14/r3.speaker: author
TABRISI:43:11-14/r3.claim: God sends rain in the amount needed, neither excessive nor insufficient; this shows a powerful, choosing agent who measures by wisdom and knowledge.
TABRISI:43:11-14/r3.anchor: بقدر الحاجة لا زائدا عليها فيفسد ولا ناقصا عنها فيضر ولا ينفع

TABRISI:43:11-14/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:43:11-14/r4.speaker: author
TABRISI:43:11-14/r4.claim: Rain revives dry land with plants, trees, crops, and fruit; similarly, people will emerge from their graves at resurrection.
TABRISI:43:11-14/r4.anchor: أي جافة يابسة بإخراج النبات والأشجار والزروع والثمار

THALABI:v8p328/r11.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v8p328/r11.speaker: author
THALABI:v8p328/r11.claim: God sends rain in the amount people need; with it He revives dead land, just as people will be raised alive from their graves.
THALABI:v8p328/r11.anchor: والذي نزل من السماء ماء بقدر أي بمقدار حاجتكم إليه.

THALABI:v8p328/r12.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v8p328/r12.speaker: author
THALABI:v8p328/r12.claim: Just as rain revives dead land, the dead will come out alive from their graves.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p15#2/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p15#2/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p15#2/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas contrasts measured rain for people's and animals' livelihood with the unmeasured flood sent to Noah's people, which drowned and destroyed them.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p15#2/r1.anchor: قال ابن عباس: يريد # ليس كما أنزل على قوم نوح بغير قدر حتى أغرقهم

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:43:11-13/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:43:11-13/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:43:11-13/r1.claim: God sends water in a measure known to Him.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:43:11-13/r1.anchor: والذي نزل من السماء ماء بقدر } بمقدار معلوم عند الله

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:43:11-13/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:43:11-13/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:43:11-13/r2.claim: God revives a dead land with the water, just as people will be brought alive from their graves.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:43:11-13/r2.anchor: فأنشرنا } فأحيينا { به } بذلك الماء { بلدة ميتا كذلك تخرجون } من قبوركم أحياء

ELMALILI:43:1-15#2/r12.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:43:1-15#2/r12.speaker: author
ELMALILI:43:1-15#2/r12.claim: The divine descriptions clarify who God is; the shift from third person to first person in the revival statement signals this clarification.
ELMALILI:43:1-15#2/r12.anchor: Allah teâlâ tarafından tavzihtir. Böyle olduğuna karîne olmak üzere gıyabdan tekellüme iltifat

ELMALILI:43:1-15#2/r13.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:43:1-15#2/r13.speaker: author
ELMALILI:43:1-15#2/r13.claim: As rain revives a dead town, so God will bring people to new life—through the Qur’an as a spirit, or by raising them from graves; the power that revived can do this too.

MAJAZ:v2p202/r1.author: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar b. al-Muthannā
MAJAZ:v2p202/r1.speaker: author
MAJAZ:v2p202/r1.claim: Ansharnā means ‘revived’; an earth that nasharat has come back to life. Al-Aʿshā’s line ‘the dead one revived’ attests the sense.
MAJAZ:v2p202/r1.anchor: «فأنشرنا به بلدة ميتا» (11) أي أحيينا ونشرت الأرض أي حييت قال الأعشى:

RUMMANI:v1p89/r3.author: al-Rummānī
RUMMANI:v1p89/r3.speaker: author
RUMMANI:v1p89/r3.claim: أَنشَرْنَا figuratively means that vegetation, trees, and fruits appear; the dead town is treated as resurrected, a stronger image than mere showing.
RUMMANI:v1p89/r3.anchor: أظهرنا به النبات والأشجار والثمار فكانت كمن أحييناه بعد إماتته

DAMGHANI:v1p453/r15.author: al-Dāmghānī
DAMGHANI:v1p453/r15.speaker: author
DAMGHANI:v1p453/r15.claim: Nashr can mean bringing life: rain revives a dead land, like life after death.
DAMGHANI:v1p453/r15.anchor: فوجه منها النشور الحياة قوله تعالى في سورة الزخرف فأنشرنا به بلدة ميتا
